Ah, nevermind then. The FX 6350 is still a pretty good processor, specially for gaming. You will see some better CPU usage if you are using DX12 or Vulkan in most cases. Vulkan isn't entirely here yet, but it's the OpenGL version of DX12 and Mantle so it should work on a lot more than Windows 10 like DX12.

I usually stagger my CPU+motherboard+ram and graphics cards updates too, and upgrade one or the other every few years. I find it's a better way to get more for your money and to eventually work up to a high end rig. Most people say CPU bottlenecks aren't good, but I've had them in the past. And when you stagger upgrades, it makes the CPU+motherboard+ram upgrade a lot more impactful. I don't think it's as bad as people say, I just turned up MSAA. Or, if you're CPU bottlenecked, you can always increase resolution. Though I wouldn't go past 1440p with the 480.

Probably not a very popular opinion to bottleneck by CPU, but if you're going to hold onto the graphics card for a while and you'll update the rest of your system beforehand, it's usually worth it.

I think that 480 would last you well into your next CPU upgrade. The AMD GCN cards tend to age well. I still have my 7970 and I'm happy with it, and I've had it longer than I've ever had a graphics card. For $240 the 8GB card is a really good deal, and the 4GB is a good deal for $200 too.

We don't usually get new releases like this that offer this kind of performance per dollar, specially when moving to a new process (we went from 28nm to 14nm). Usually they cost a ton more, like when 7970 was $550 at launch.

The current FX-series CPUs are not very good. AMD is going to release 14nm Zen later this year, which will probably be much better. Apparently the first Zens will be high performance desktop CPUs, so I don't know if those are the ones you're looking for. There is reason to believe, however, that the release of Zen is going to cut prices, so if you can wait for at least 5 months before buying a new CPU, I would wait.
